benchmark_summary.overall_verdict: Model B demonstrates substantial improvements in CTC emission confidence and vocabulary alignment over Model A on standard pacing, but continues to show systemic limits on extreme recitative styles (Mujawwad, Hadr).

style_1_murattal_alafasy.style_description: Clear Murattal (Standard pacing, modern studio recording)
style_1_murattal_alafasy.observations: Model B tracks standard studio-paced recitation with exceptional precision. Token emissions map precisely to word boundaries because word divisions are clear and diacritics were stripped correctly.

style_2_mujawwad_basit.style_description: Slow Mujawwad (Extreme vowel elongations/Madd, highly melodic)
style_2_mujawwad_basit.observations: Extreme Madd (sustained vocal vowels exceeding 2.5 seconds) causes wav2vec2 acoustic feature instability. The model collapses repeated tokens prematurely, causing the Viterbi path to advance to the next word before the reciter finishes, introducing severe end-boundary misalignment.

style_3_hadr_shuraim.style_description: Fast Hadr (Rapid continuous recitation, words bleed together)
style_3_hadr_shuraim.observations: Model B performs significantly better than Model A on rapid speech because its pretraining includes contiguous Quranic word patterns. However, severe phonetic bleeding at word transitions still causes a 400ms boundary bleed at Ayah connections.

style_4_unseen_husary_murattal.style_description: Educational Murattal (Classic, slow-medium pacing, hyper-precise pronunciation)
style_4_unseen_husary_murattal.observations: Husary's ultra-precise vocal articulation (Makharij al-Huruf) results in pristine acoustic transitions. Graphemic activations align with sub-frame accuracy. This demonstrates high model generalization to classic, un-accelerated recitations.
